items.title: In Nepal, Picking Up Dog Shit Is Still a Caste Problem | Dr. Julie Palais, Animal-Law Advocate
items.description:
Julie Palais: "The dogs are below even the lowest people in society." From a Jeep-window contrast — wealthy pet with tika vs street dogs — into responsible ownership: feeding isn't enough. When she mentions picking up after a dog on a walk, people in Nepal are horrified — the unspoken caste logic of who handles waste. items.title: Make PE Richer, or Fix the Family Business? | Lowell Mora, Fractional CFO
items.description:
After selling into strategic buyers and private equity, Lowell Mora flipped the model: rather than making PE guys richer, help real owners and the people who've worked those shops for decades. Owners always overvalue the business; he comes in for years, grows EBITDA, then sits on their side of the table at exit — retainer, not a skim of the sale. And why "fractional CFO" is booming while the market is still flooded with people selling accounting as strategy.

items.description:
Owners often "know" their business cold — until the margins say otherwise. Fractional CFO Lowell Mora (Impact CFO) on the pattern he kept seeing across 30+ years: people had about ten things they knew; typically eight and a half were right — and the gaps lived in customer and product margin minutia. Why a CFO lens helps when you can hire a controller but not a full-time CFO — and why family businesses that refuse debt (or drain all the cash) leave growth on the table.

items.title: Table Stakes: Just Show Up | Preeti Varma, NYC artist
items.description:
What if the hard part of being an artist isn't finding inspiration — it's just showing up? Preeti Varma (NYC artist) answers my question about whether you have to force evolution or let it happen: both. The studio is where things happen naturally — but only if you're there every day. Discipline as table stakes. Then the other half: museums, history, showing up for friends' openings, community. And a third: time alone to assimilate, so looking doesn't erase originality.
